To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CD4+ T regulatory lymphocytes are a diverse group of cells that can suppress immune responses in a number of ways.

CD4+ T regulatory (Treg) cells have a fundamental role to play in the establishment and/or maintenance of peripheral tolerance, and that manipulating the numbers of Treg cells can decrease pathology in humans in a wide range diseases.

T regulatory cell (Treg) based therapies are likely to be effective in human diseases, and that we need to understand the characteristics of different human Treg populations to design the best therapies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the biology of human regulatory T cells, and the development of novel strategies to harness their therapeutic potential.

there is a need to understand the role of T regulatory cells and their subsets in human diseases, in particular autoimmune and cancer.

the CD4 Tregs are a heterogeneous population of regulatory cells that are critical to maintaining self tolerance and preventing immune pathology in humans.
Tregs are an attractive therapeutic target for a wide range of diseases, and that the next decade will provide the first clinical trials of Tregs in humans.
Tregs can be expanded in vitro from peripheral blood and that this expansion is associated with a significant increase in the frequency of Tregs.
